lesson: When two views compute the 'same' metric at different grains, the first hypothesis to test is filter-scope mismatch: does each view apply its lifetime / tenure filter at the SAME grain as its row key? Confirm by SELECT COUNT(*) ... WHERE filter_a != filter_b at the join grain before suggesting a fix.
evidence: EDAEM-3772 root cause: arr_product_customer_retention_dashboard filtered customer_lifetime at product grain (wd_customer_lifetime_qtr) while the incremental view filtered at account grain (customers_total_lifetime_qtr). Excluded long-tenured accounts whose new products had low product-lifetime (Evisort acquisition, PharmaCord expansion).

lesson: Always validate fix hypotheses through Snowflake MCP before posting to Jira. The validation query should return the rows the fix would RECOVER (e.g. 'accounts excluded today that would be included after the swap'). Quantify the impact (account count, ARR magnitude) in the RCA comment so the requester can sanity-check it without a re-run.
evidence: EDAEM-3772 RCA comment cited specific PharmaCord / Evisort accounts with row counts and product-lifetime values; the requester accepted the fix on first read.

lesson: `debugger` paused with: "Approve to post Bug-shaped debug comment to EDAEM-3772". Resolve this kind of ambiguity earlier (clarifier or analyser) so the DAG keeps moving.
evidence: debugger returned `needs_input` in run for EDAEM-3772: target=arr_customer_retention_dashboard trigger=cli lineage_nodes=1 stage_checks=1 hypotheses=1 top=medium issue_type=Bug

lesson: BFS-walks upstream lineage of target_model via ripgrep on `ref()` calls (no `dbt list` needed; works without a compiled project). Depth cap = 5. Produces: LineageNode[], ValidationMatrix (one row per lineage node, 7-col shape), ACAnalysis[] (one row per acceptance criterion), ranked RootCauseHypothesis[], ProposedFix (file + LLM prompt - NEVER writes the change itself), and a PytestHarnessSpec under tests/pytest/ (both .gitignored).

Jira ADF comment shape is ticket-type-aware: Bug -> 'Root cause + reproducible fix' + Repro steps + Regression test. Story/Task/Sub-task/Epic -> 'Debug findings' + Suggested investigation focus. Always pause before posting unless auth_mode = FULL_AUTO.

PBU-Manual records pattern (a known RCA shortcut): when PVQ-vs-QA mismatch rows are 100% concentrated in `agree_data_migrations = 'NonMigrated-PBU-Manual'` with PVQ stage_name='9- Closed/Won' and QA stage_name=NULL, the root cause is the UNION trick in `stg_em_opp_source_temp.sql` (the `LEFT JOIN ... LIMIT 0` against COMMON_SOURCE structurally drops Account attributes for PBU rows). QA's surrogate-key join architecture is actually CORRECT here - PVQ/Prod is structurally deficient. Fix: hardcode the PBU stage_name fallback in QA; leave PARENT_ACCOUNT_NAME alone (QA is right).
evidence: Refactored QA / UAT Testing - 24,140 mismatches, 100% PBU-Manual, full RCA documented.

lesson: Before declaring a refactor regression, ALWAYS check if QA is actually IMPROVING coverage vs Prod. QA's surrogate-key joins achieved 99.97% fidelity to Salesforce for `parent_account_name` on PBU records where Prod/PVQ return NULL for all 5,261 PBU accounts. A 'mismatch' isn't always a bug - sometimes the refactor fixes a long-standing prod deficiency. Include a 'QA improvements over Prod' subsection in the RCA so the requester sees the upside.
evidence: Refactored QA / UAT Testing - parent_account_name analysis conclusion.

lesson: Sourcing-change recon: when a refactor changes the source of a derived column (e.g. `term_start`/`term_end` moves from `bt_sku_analytics` join in PVQ to `finance_line_data` via `finance_line_analytics` join in QA), values may differ even though logic is equivalent. Validate at agreement grain via Snowflake before opening a regression ticket: run both join expressions inline as CTEs and diff the (term_start, term_end) pairs.
evidence: Refactored QA / UAT Testing - $141K ARR shifted between ssr_off_cycle and off_cycle for a1X4X000007UyvvUAC.

lesson: Revert PR title convention: 'Revert <thing> (PRs #X, #Y)' OR 'Roll back #X' OR '<feature> (revert PR #X)'. Always cite the reverted PR numbers in the title so git log + gh pr list remains searchable. Examples in window: #316 (reverts #313/#314/#315), #354 (removes #326), #420 (reverts #414), #457 (rolls back #450/#454/#453), #443/#444 (surgical rollback of #441).

Prefer SURGICAL rollback over wholesale revert when only one change in a multi-change PR went wrong. PR #443 kept the case-fix and alias hygiene from #441/#442 but reverted ONLY the `>= 4` → `> 4` lifetime-qtr filter change — labelled '**Surgical rollback**' in the body with a clear 'What changed in PR #N (yesterday)' table marking each change as 'Reverted' / 'Preserved'.

When a Slack flag from a finance stakeholder lands (e.g. Svet's $524M NRR Q4 discrepancy at 9:10 AM PT 2026-05-13 in #enterprise-metrics-fusion-team), the same-day rollback playbook is: (1) reproduce the discrepancy in certified_qa, (2) write a surgical-rollback PR with the validation table BEFORE/AFTER, (3) quote the Slack flag verbatim in the PR body, (4) open the prod promotion PR same-day with 'DO NOT MERGE until QA PR #N validated' gate. Pattern from #443/#444 closed inside 24 hours.

Reverts in window (Apr-Jun 2026): 5 distinct revert events on qa, all 5 promoted to prod. Risk areas (where reverts cluster): (1) CI/CD workflow infra (#316), (2) speculative architecture refactors (#354 pipeline-runner, #457 nested-function-call removal), (3) business-rule date filters (#420 term_end backdate, #443 lifetime-qtr filter). Lesson: large architectural PRs and date-filter changes need extra qa validation time.

PR #457 'Roll back #450/#454/#453; re-add wd_agreement* models + #453 perf tuning' shows the canonical hybrid-rollback recipe when three stacked PRs partially work: (1) revert all three, (2) keep the bits that ARE good (the 5 standalone wd_agreement* models from #454), (3) re-apply the perf tuning from #453 on top. Document the net delta with explicit 'Reverted / Removed / Re-added / Re-applied' bullets so reviewers can map commits → outcomes.

Six PRs in 6 days (Apr 1-6: #308, #309, #312, #328, #330, plus a later #412 ref-resolution fix) all stemmed from float-precision issues in the arr_categories UDF chain. When you see one float-precision bug in this codebase, GREP the entire functions/ + macros/em/ tree for similar `!= 0` / `>= X` / cast-to-int patterns — they tend to be systemic, not isolated.

Hybrid-rollback recipe (canonicalized by #457): in one PR — (1) full revert of the bad set as commit 1 (verify byte-for-byte vs the pre-bad baseline SHA), (2) chore: remove any other legacy fallouts as commit 2, (3) feat: re-add the keep-worthy pieces as commit 3, (4) perf: re-apply tunings as commit 4. PR body must have explicit 'Reverted / Removed / Re-added / Re-applied' bullets so reviewers can map commits → outcomes without reading the diff.
evidence: eda-dbt-em PR walk 2026-06-25 (post-IA window: qa #449→#472, prod #459→#465); FLA upstream tree = 43 EM models + 15 cross-project + 2 external dims.

lesson: Pending-renewal bug: an expired agreement's EB ARR is not cleared when a signed short-term extension exists in the SAME fiscal quarter, so both carry forward (DSW: +$1.8M NE, +$3.6M EB). Resolve via per-account override.

Outliers are non-diagnostic. A large contraction/expansion is not inherently an error (T-Mobile -$7.2M = all contracts legitimately expired). Always include date fields in outlier analysis; if contracts expire on schedule, there is no error.

Overrides placed UPSTREAM of the up-for-renewal / price-quantity functions can double-count agreement ARR (DIA off-cycle, 5/11). Reconciliation identity: Up for Renewal + Off-Cycle + SSR Up for Renewal + SSR Off-Cycle + Off-Cycle No Activity = ARR USD Current.

SCENARIO: category counts look wrong while ARR/FSE tie out. ROOT CAUSE: intentional $0 ARR records in Expansion/Contraction (PvQ attribution + $0 extensions). RESOLUTION: keep them; only remove $0 records that neither start nor expire. Never delete $0 rows wholesale.

SCENARIO: unexplained large EB jump across a close (e.g. +$95M). ROOT CAUSE: constant-currency FX rate reset (FY26->FY27: EUR -8.8%, GBP -3.8%, CHF -8.8%), not a logic bug. RESOLUTION: rule out FX first; announced '$X change' figures often already include the reset.

SCENARIO: inflated churn/expansion 'variance' (~$15M) from an ad-hoc query. ROOT CAUSE: ARR aggregated on a raw column instead of split_arr_usd_current, double-counting split/partner deals. RESOLUTION: re-aggregate on split_arr_usd_current.

SCENARIO: false Expansion (DSW +$3.6M EB / +$1.8M NE). ROOT CAUSE: pending-renewal did not clear an expired agreement because a signed short-term extension existed in the same fiscal quarter; amendment not handled by ARR logic. RESOLUTION: per-account override (isolated; no other accounts impacted).

SCENARIO: large contraction flagged as an error (T-Mobile -$7.2M). ROOT CAUSE: contracts legitimately expired on schedule (no terminations). RESOLUTION: non-diagnostic - include date fields; if expiries are on schedule, there is no bug.

SCENARIO: agreement ARR double-counts after an override (DIA off-cycle, 5/11). ROOT CAUSE: override placed UPSTREAM of the up-for-renewal / price-quantity functions. RESOLUTION: place overrides downstream; verify identity Up for Renewal + Off-Cycle + SSR Up for Renewal + SSR Off-Cycle + Off-Cycle No Activity = ARR USD Current.

SCENARIO: $36M ACV shows as $51M ARR across products (DIA/WGC). ROOT CAUSE: quote/agreement mismatch, SKU ACV reallocated by buying-center, bespoke partner resale (Groundswell). RESOLUTION: override to $36M to match RevRec schedule. Note ACV can be Add-On while ARR is Net Expansion.

SCENARIO: M&A ARR differs wildly between systems (Paradox $123M Prism vs $18M Sigma; +$105M EB). ROOT CAUSE: ARR filters out pre-acquisition activity via legacy SKUs, but source rows remain and Prism/Adaptive reads source directly. RESOLUTION: pre-acquisition excluded from ARR/GRR/NRR is correct; Prism is downstream, not ED&A-owned.

SCENARIO: an acquired-standalone account flags FALSE for Standalone Acc Buy Wd Products (Evisort/HiredScore). ROOT CAUSE: acquisition hard-coded in 4-5 code places; one was missed. RESOLUTION: drive off Reltio Source Entity (entity source != Workday and != B2B) instead of per-acquisition lists.

SCENARIO: ACV won't tie to ARR by segment. ROOT CAUSE: a 50/50 opportunity split across two segments (e.g. Partner + North America) defaults the whole agreement to one segment because ARR consolidates at agreement grain. RESOLUTION: expected behavior; reconcile at agreement grain, not segment.

SCENARIO: an account keeps ARR in 'Partnerships' after a strategic-partner seed change (Proquire ~$63k). ROOT CAUSE: that ARR is driven by partner_type (Innovation/Channel Partner from partner_track/opportunity_segment), not is_strategic_partner/business_segment. RESOLUTION: adjust the partner_type rule or exclude the product; a strategic-partner seed update will not move it.

SCENARIO: FSE counts materially off historically (Walmart/Hitachi). ROOT CAUSE: amendments not applied by FSE logic; source quantity/UOM/term unowned & unvalidated. RESOLUTION: treat as outliers - no cleanup path without an operations owner.

SCENARIO: product churn/swaps missing from NRR/GRR in a product's first year for a tenured account. ROOT CAUSE: the <12-month PRODUCT lifetime filter (filter #3) wrongly applied to non-acquisition products. RESOLUTION: remove filter #3 for non-acquisition products; keep M&A exclusion; acquisition quarter filter is >4 not >=4.
SCENARIO: Net New/Add-On ARR appears for records with IS ARR = False (Sana services SKUs). ROOT CAUSE: services SKUs not excluded. RESOLUTION: exclude services SKUs (fixed 5/9).

ACV 'evenly distributed across all SKUs' for an opp means the source agreement lines do NOT sum to the opp/header amount (no-fee/limited-use SKUs zeroed, or lines > header), so ACV gets refactored and spread evenly. Confirm by comparing sum(acv__c) on base_prod.salesforce.apttus__agreementlineitem__c for the agreement vs opp ACV in bv_sku_acv. Example: agreement a1XVT00000Dxtc52AB summed to ~$727,949 while opp 006VT00000oOR77YAG ACV was $126,600.60 -> 17 SKUs each exactly $7,447.09. Fix at source (line<->header tie-out); do not override. SCOPE: ACV/bookings consumer-support context (Sales Finance <-> ED&A), distinct from the IA/FLA ARR scope; do not apply legacy ACV table logic when working strictly inside the IA project.

lesson: SKU value doubles / opp overstated after an override = duplicate SKU rows (SSR 2-row pattern: one net-delta row, one $0 placeholder). The override join on (opp, as_was_date, sku) fans out across both base rows (2x2 cartesian). Recommended fix: do NOT override the duplicated SKU (base net is already correct), or code-fix to aggregate the seed before joining. Example opp 006VT00000VY6ltYAD (HCM, TT). lesson: Opp missing from the ACV table, or ACV defaulting to 'Workday Services', usually means NO primary/approved quote (also: deleted proposal/quote-line in SFDC, or an M&A product with no exception). Without a primary quote, ACV can't be allocated to SKUs and falls back to workday_services__c (which may not list the acquired SKU, e.g. Paradox/LDPCEXP) or the opp drops entirely. Fix primary quote at source, add product exception, or use the appends list. lesson: Day-1 quarter results understated in BV_FINANCE_OPPORTUNITY_SKU_QUOTE_LINE_DAILY_SNAPSHOT vs BV_ACV_QUOTELINE_NEW_HIERARCHY: the daily snapshot is captured EOD PST, so end-of-last-day stage flips to Won land in the NEXT day's snapshot, and some opps drop out of the snapshot after their last active day.
